extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in differential geometry / geometric analysis
extracted.subtask_short: short-time Ricci flow existence and estimates
extracted.subtask_description: Establish short-time existence/uniqueness for the Ricci flow (compact and noncompact cases), derive evolution equations for curvature, and obtain derivative (Shi) estimates; also introduce Perelman's variational functionals and their monotonicity under a coupled flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak parabolicity of Ricci flow (cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ricci flow is a system of second order nonlinear weakly parabolic PDEs; the degeneracy (zero eigenvalues of the principal symbol) is caused by the diffeomorphism group of M acting as a gauge group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the linearization DE(g) and its symbol σDE(g)(ζ) to see zero eigenvectors corresponding to variations generated by diffeomorphisms; this observation motivates gauge fixing (DeTurck trick).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbol computation of linearization
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbol of DE(gij) in direction ζ is σDE(g)(ζ)˜gij = gkl(ζiζj˜gkl + ζkζl˜gij − ζiζk˜gjl − ζjζk˜gil).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing coordinates with gij = δij and ζ = (1,0,...,0) yields explicit zero-eigenvectors; use this to identify the degeneracy directions (diffeomorphisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: DeTurck gauge-fixing to obtain strict parabolicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce a family of diffeomorphisms ϕt and consider the pull-back metric gij = ϕt* ĝij; choose the flow for ϕt by an ODE so that the modified metric flow becomes strictly parabolic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define vector field Vi = gik gjl(Γk_jl − Γ̊k_jl) where Γ̊ is the connection of the initial metric; then the modified evolution ∂t gij = −2Rij + ∇iVj + ∇jVi is strictly parabolic (symbol gkl ζk ζl ˜gij). Solve this strictly parabolic system and recover solutions of original Ricci flow by pulling back via solutions of the ODE for ϕt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-time existence and uniqueness on compact manifolds (Theorem 1.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (M, gij(x)) be a compact Riemannian manifold. There exists T>0 such that the initial value problem ∂t gij = −2Rij, gij(·,0)=gij has a unique smooth solution gij(x,t) on M × [0,T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DeTurck's trick to transform to a strictly parabolic equation (existence via standard parabolic theory) and then use ODE uniqueness for the diffeomorphism flow to obtain uniqueness for the Ricci flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shi's short-time existence on complete noncompact manifolds (Theorem 1.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (M,gij) is a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold of dimension n with bounded curvature, then there exists T>0 such that the Ricci flow initial value problem has a smooth solution gij(x,t) on M × [0,T] with uniformly bounded curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The noncompact case requires substantial PDE techniques; Shi's thesis (1989) constructs the short-time solution with curvature bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness on noncompact manifolds requires bounded curvature (Chen–Zhu, Theorem 1.2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (M, ĝij) be a complete noncompact Riemannian manifold with bounded curvature. If gij(x,t) and ġij(x,t) are two solutions on M×[0,T] to Ricci flow with the same initial data and both have bounded curvature, then they are identical on M×[0,T].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness for heat-type equations on noncompact manifolds can fail without growth restrictions; bounded curvature is the reasonable/essential growth condition to guarantee uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution equation for the Riemann curvature tensor (Proposition 1.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Ricci flow ∂t gij = −2Rij, the curvature tensor evolves by ∂t Rijkl = ∆Rijkl + 2(Bijkl − Bijlk − Biljk + Bikjl) + gpq(RpjklRqi + RipklRqj + RijplRqk + RijkpRql), where Bijkl = gpr gqs Rpiqj Rrksl and ∆ is the Laplacian of the evolving metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a nonlinear reaction–diffusion (heat-type) PDE for curvature; use normal coordinates and Bianchi identities in derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution of Ricci tensor and scalar curvature (Corollaries 1.3.2 & 1.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ricci evolves by ∂t Rik = ∆Rik + 2 gpr gqs Rpiqk Rrs − 2 g^{pq} R_{p i} R_{q k}. Scalar curvature evolves by ∂t R = ∆R + 2 |Ric|^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These follow from contracting the curvature evolution and using Bianchi identities; they are used in maximum principle arguments for curvature quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing curvature as an operator on 2-forms (Rm as bilinear form) and matrix evolution (Proposition 1.3.4 / (1.3.9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent Rabcd = M_{αβ} ϕ^α_{ab} ϕ^β_{cd} on Λ^2; then M_{αβ} satisfies ∂t M_{αβ} = ∆M_{αβ} + (M^2)_{αβ} + M^{#}_{αβ}, where (M^2)_{αβ} = M_{αγ}M_{βγ} and M^{#} is the Lie-algebraic adjoint-type quadratic term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reformulation clarifies the quadratic (reaction) terms using algebraic structure of Λ^2 and Lie brackets; useful for dimension-specific curvature pinching analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension-specific structure: M# in 3D and block decomposition in 4D
rubrics_metrics.description: In dimension 3, M^{#} is the adjugate of M (M^{#} = det(M) (M^{-1})^T). In dimension 4, using Hodge decomposition Λ^2 = Λ^2_+ ⊕ Λ^2_- the curvature operator matrix M decomposes into blocks A, B, C and M^{#} has a corresponding block adjoint structure (see (1.3.11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These algebraic identities give concrete formulas for the quadratic terms, used in 3- and 4-dimensional curvature analyses (e.g., Hamilton's pinching results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Shi derivative estimates (Theorem 1.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist constants C_m (m ≥ 1) depending only on dimension such that: if a complete solution to Ricci flow has |Rm| ≤ M up to time t with 0 < t ≤ 1/M, then |∇Rm| ≤ C_1 M / √t and more generally |∇^m Rm| ≤ C_m M / t^{m/2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are global Bernstein-type parabolic derivative estimates: curvature bounds at positive times control all spatial derivatives (powers of t in denominator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Shi derivative estimates (Theorem 1.4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist θ, C_k (depending only on dimension) such that: if |Rm| ≤ M on an open set U×[0,θ/M], B_0(p,r) ⊂ U and r ≤ θ/√M, then at (p,t) for 0<t≤θ/M one has (schematically) |∇^k Rm(p,t)|^2 ≤ C_k M^2 (1/r^{2k} + 1/t^k + M^k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives local-in-space versions of Shi estimates (with cut-off functions and barrier arguments). Use when only local curvature control is available; constants depend only on dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: parabolic maximum principle with barrier functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive derivative bounds by forming appropriate quantities F (combining derivatives weighted by powers of t and curvature), computing ∂t − ∆ of F, and applying the parabolic maximum principle with carefully chosen cutoff/barrier functions (ϕ) supported in balls B_0(p,r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses evolution inequalities for |∇^k Rm|^2, Cauchy inequalities, and construction of H (barrier) so that ∂t H > ∆H − H^2 + M^2; then compare F and H to obtain bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of breather and relation to Ricci solitons (Definition 1.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric gij(t) evolving by Ricci flow is a breather if for some t1<t2 and α>0 the metrics α gij(t1) and gij(t2) differ only by a diffeomorphism; α=1,α<1,α>1 correspond to steady, shrinking, expanding breathers. Ricci solitons are trivial breathers (metrics differ by diffeomorphism and scaling for every pair t1,t2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breathers are analogues of periodic orbits modulo diffeomorphism and scaling; classification results often show breathers must be solitons under additional hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's F-functional definition (1.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman's F functional is F(g,f) = ∫_M (R + |∇f|^2) e^{-f} dV, defined on pairs (g,f) where f is a smooth function on compact M and R is scalar curvature of g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: F is a useful Lyapunov-type functional for Ricci flow modulo diffeomorphism; variations of F yield Euler-Lagrange-type tensors Rij + ∇i∇j f.

rubrics_metrics.name: First variation of Perelman's F-functional (Lemma 1.5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If δg_{ij}=v_{ij}, δf = h, then δF(v,h) = ∫_M [ −h (R + |∇f|^2 − 2 ∆f) + v^{ij}(−R_{ij} − ∇i∇j f) + (v/2) (R + |∇f|^2) ] e^{-f} dV (schematic; see lemma for exact formula).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical points (stationary under variations preserving ∫ e^{-f} dV) are steady gradient Ricci solitons satisfying Rij + ∇i∇j f = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of F under coupled flow and strictness criterion (Proposition 1.5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the coupled flow ∂t g_{ij} = −2 R_{ij}, ∂t f = −∆f + |∇f|^2 − R, one has d/dt F(g(t),f(t)) = 2 ∫_M |R_{ij} + ∇i∇j f|^2 e^{-f} dV ≥ 0. Monotonicity is strict unless (M,g,f) is a steady gradient soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows F is nondecreasing along this coupled evolution and constant precisely on steady gradient solitons; also ∫_M e^{-f} dV is preserved along the coupled flow.
